name: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II
platform: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox, BASS flow duct (7.6 cm square)
summary: Small flow-duct burns of solid fuels in microgravity with oxygen lowered by nitrogen dilution. Measured flame spread, extinction by quenching and blowoff, and combustion products. The only investigation here with verified test-level data in this service.

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
platform: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox, BASS flow duct
summary: Predecessor to BASS-II on the same hardware: 115 burns on 41 samples. Established strong flame sensitivity to flow below 5 cm/s and long-lived dim flames below 1 cm/s.

name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment I-III
platform: Uncrewed Cygnus vehicle, Saffire flow unit (46 cm duct)
materials: silicone, SIBAL, Nomex, PMMA 5 cm wide (II)
summary: First large-scale fires set inside a spacecraft. Measured spread over a fabric sheet an order of magnitude larger than earlier microgravity samples, and material flammability (II).

name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment IV and V
platform: Uncrewed Cygnus vehicle (NG-13, NG-14), Saffire flow unit (30 cm duct for IV)
variables: forced flow 20 cm/s, reduced and stopped in some tests
summary: Large-scale fires on thick fuels and in exploration-like atmospheres, with vehicle impact, extinguishment by reducing or stopping flow, and surface-structure effects.

name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction - Growth and Extinction Limit
summary: Extinction limits of thick PMMA spheres in a different apparatus from BASS-II. Five extinction cases detail quenching, blowoff and the transition between them.

name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
platform: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack, Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus
variables: O2 with N2, CO2 and He dilution
summary: Droplet combustion and extinction under inert-gas dilution. The report catalogues results without interpreting them. Liquid fuels, so not comparable with solid-fuel spread.

name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight
summary: Smoke particle size from overheated, non-flaming spacecraft materials, for fire detector design. No flames.
